technical_hypothesis.interaction_pattern: real-time or near-real-time human-reviewed alert prioritization
technical_hypothesis.primary_training_data_risk: the operating envelope changes with new products, customer life events, campaigns, fraud adaptation, regulation and incident response, producing unstable baselines and high false-positive risk

training_data.observation_unit: one transaction, entity-time window, settlement interval or claim relationship at the review cutoff
training_data.input_data: pre-cutoff values, frequencies, device or channel context, counterparties, account history, peer group, graph relationships and system-health signals; availability varies by institution
training_data.target_or_reward: human-confirmed unusual or actionable case and downstream investigation outcome; unsupervised training does not require labels, but thresholding and evaluation do
training_data.label_source: fraud, AML, treasury, claims, incident and case-management review outcomes; consistency and linkage are unknown
training_data.prediction_time: before authorization when permitted, or before analyst prioritization and operational escalation
training_data.class_balance: unknown; actionable anomalies are expected to be rare
training_data.historical_coverage: unknown; regime, product, channel and fraud-pattern changes reduce comparability
training_data.train_validation_split: time-based backtesting across regime changes, products and channels, with entity-group holdouts where transfer is claimed
training_data.leakage_risks: using investigation outcomes, blocks, chargebacks, MED results, corrected positions, claim decisions or post-review graph edges created after the cutoff
training_data.representativeness_risks: customer segments, regions, channels, products, institution size, fraud campaigns, catastrophes and market calendars differ materially
training_data.feedback_loop: alerts change blocks, analyst attention and customer behavior, altering the future baseline and observed outcomes
training_data.privacy_and_usage_constraints: financial and behavioral data require purpose limitation, minimization, strict access, auditability and controls against discriminatory peer grouping
training_data.fallback_if_data_is_insufficient: use deterministic limits, velocity and scenario rules, reconciliations, sanctions and fraud controls, supervised models where labels exist, and specialist review

portfolio_comparison.reason: Pix behavioral and graph anomaly detection is already central to FIN-001, claim relationship anomalies are represented in FIN-002, and generic transaction or liquidity anomaly monitoring does not expose a distinct bounded outcome beyond current regulatory controls and mature monitoring platforms.

existing_landscape.summary: Adopt or extend existing fraud, AML, treasury, claims and observability platforms with institution-specific rules and governed anomaly models; do not create a separate generic anomaly opportunity.

research.findings: Current Banco Central rules require continuous real-time monitoring of atypical or fraudulent transactions using historical and behavioral patterns, and the regulator already performs broad anomaly-oriented monitoring of the financial system. The mechanism is important but already represented in FIN-001 and mature fraud, AML and risk-monitoring capabilities. Microsoft also retires the standalone Azure Anomaly Detector service on 1 October 2026, reinforcing use of broader Fabric or custom/open-source implementations rather than a new standalone reference opportunity.

where_ai_enters.primary_mechanism: detect multivariate, peer-group or graph deviations not covered by deterministic scenarios and prioritize specialist review
where_ai_enters.human_control: fraud, AML, treasury, claims and risk specialists retain blocking, reporting, investigation, customer-impact and regulatory decisions
